## Verdict: **fix_first**

This is a fairly standard "meme token with tax + anti-bot" contract. It's not an outright scam (no hidden mint, no blacklist function that can seize arbitrary wallets, no honeypot on normal transfers), but there are several real bugs and dangerous design issues that should be addressed before deployment.

---

## Issues Found

### 1. Line ~318–330 — Broken/duplicated swap logic in `_transfer`
The `else if` branch is dead code in practice: the `if` and `else if` have **identical conditions** (`!inSwap && marketPair[to] && swapEnabled && contractTokenBalance>_taxSwapThreshold && _buyCount>_preventSwapBefore`). The `else if` will only be reached if the first `if`'s body reverts — but it can't, because `require(sellCount < sellsPerBlock)` at line ~322 **reverts the entire transfer** rather than skipping. So the "else if" fallback (which looks like it was meant to be the "we haven't hit the per-block sell limit yet" path) is unreachable. Result: once `sellCount >= sellsPerBlock` in a block, **all sells revert**.

**Impact:** Griefing vector. An attacker can spam small sells at the start of a block to fill `sellCount`, then every subsequent sell in that block reverts. This can effectively brick trading in a block.

### 2. Lines ~299 / ~307 — `isExile` used as both "no-tax" and "no-max" bypass
`isExile` is set on `owner`, `address(this)`, and `uniswapV2Pair` in the constructor (lines ~226–228, ~239). Any address marked `isExile` completely skips `_maxTxAmount`, `_maxWalletSize`, and (via the `!isExile[to]` checks) tax. There is no way for holders to add or remove from this set after deployment, which is good — but the naming is misleading (it's actually a whitelist, not a blacklist) and it means `owner` and the pair are permanently exempted. Worth confirming this is intended.

### 3. Line ~311–313 — Sell tax is computed after `_buyCount` is potentially reset
Sell tax uses `_buyCount` to decide whether to apply `_finalSellTax` at `_reduceSellTaxAt=35`. But `_buyCount` is only incremented on **buys**, not sells (line ~304). So a user can trigger the tax reduction simply by other people buying. Not a bug per se, but a bit incoherent — "reduce sell tax after 35 buys" is an odd trigger. Confirm intent.

### 4. Lines ~340–352 — `rescueETH` / `rescueTokens` callable by `_taxWallet` at any time
These are unconditionally callable by `_taxWallet` (set to `_msgSender()` in constructor). Since the contract accumulates tax ETH that is meant to be swapped/distributed, a malicious or compromised `_taxWallet` can drain it instantly, bypassing the intended tax-flow. Also, `rescueTokens` has no `_tokenAddr != address(this)` guard, so it could sweep the contract's own token balance, breaking the swap logic.

### 5. Line ~233–235 — `_maxTxAmount` and `_maxWalletSize` are ~2% of supply, but initial LP is the entire supply
`enableTrading()` adds **all** `balanceOf(address(this))` as liquidity. That's fine, but note the constructor mints `_tTotal` to the deployer and never moves tokens to the contract — so `balanceOf(address(this))` at `enableTrading()` is **0** unless the owner transfers tokens in first. As written, **`enableTrading()` will add zero liquidity**, open trading on an empty pair, and `swapEnabled` becomes true. This is almost certainly a deployment-order bug: the owner expects to send tokens to the contract before calling `enableTrading()`. As written, the first `addLiquidityETH` call will succeed with 0 tokens and 0 ETH (both amounts are 0 / `address(this).balance` which may also be 0) and not actually seed a market.

**Impact:** Trading can be "enabled" on a pair with no liquidity. Anyone can then create the market themselves or the token is unbuyable. This needs to be fixed.

### 6. Lines ~336 — `swapTokensForEth` passes `amountOutMin = 0`
Sandwich/MEV exposure on every auto-swap. Standard for meme tokens but worth flagging.

### 7. Line ~233 — `uint256 private firstBlock = 0` and anti-bot check
`if(block.number == firstBlock)` (line ~293). `firstBlock` is set in `enableTrading()`, so this works only on the exact block trading opens — fine. But `perBuyCount` is keyed by block number and never cleared (line ~296), leaving permanent storage entries. Minor gas/state bloat, no security impact.

### 8. Line ~326–328 — `sellCount` / `lastSellBlock` logic
```
if (block.number > lastSellBlock) { sellCount = 0; }
require(sellCount < sellsPerBlock);
```
On the very first sell ever, `lastSellBlock = 0` and `block.number > 0`, so `sellCount` resets — OK. But if `sellsPerBlock` is meant to be a per-block rate limit, this only resets *once per new block per caller trigger*. Combined with issue #1, sells can be griefed. Consider replacing `require` with a soft skip.

### 9. No `onlyOwner` on `rescueETH` / `rescueTokens`
They gate on `_taxWallet` instead. If ownership is renounced but `_taxWallet` remains an EOA, that EOA retains the ability to drain. If `_taxWallet` is meant to be immutable, fine — but document it.

### 10. Line ~385 — `IERC20(uniswapV2Pair).approve(...)` uses `type(uint).max` for the router
Correct pattern, but note the pair address returned from `createPair` is only assigned *after* the `isExile[address(uniswapV2Pair)] = true;` line at ~237, which is a no-op (setting the zero address). Minor logic slip; the real assignment happens at line ~236 (`marketPair[address(uniswapV2Pair)] = true;`) but `isExile` for the pair is set again at ~239 correctly. Line ~237's assignment to `address(0)` is dead code.

---

## Summary of must-fix items before deploy

| # | Location | Severity | Issue |
|---|----------|----------|-------|
| 1 | ~318–330 | High | Duplicated conditions make `else if` unreachable; `require` reverts transfers instead of skipping |
| 4 | ~340–352 | High | `_taxWallet` can drain tax ETH and sweep the contract's own tokens |
| 5 | ~368–373 | High | `enableTrading()` seeds LP with `balanceOf(this)` which is 0 at that point → no real liquidity |
| 5 (cont.) | ~233–234 | High | Confirm token flow before enabling trading |
| 2 | ~299/307 | Medium | `isExile` is a permanent whitelist — document intent |
| 6 | ~336 | Medium | `amountOutMin = 0` MEV exposure |
| 9 | ~340/347 | Medium | Rescue functions gated on `_taxWallet` not `owner` |
| 7/10 | ~237, ~296 | Low | Dead code, permanent storage bloat |

**Verdict: `fix_first`** — the core token mechanics are conventional and not obviously malicious, but issues #1, #4, and #5 are concrete bugs/dangers that will either break trading or give the deployer an unfair drain capability. Do not deploy until those are addressed and the token-flow in `enableTrading` is verified.
